title: Human Evolution
topicTitle: Human evolution: position of man in animal kingdom; differences between new world monkeys and old-world monkeys, apes and man; evolution of modern man starting from anthropoid ancestor

New World monkeys differ from Old World monkeys by having:

notes: Position of humans: Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Primates, Family Hominidae, Genus Homo, Species Homo sapiens.
Primates: grasping hands, forward-facing eyes, large brain; include prosimii (lemurs), monkeys, apes, and humans.
New World vs Old World monkeys: New World (Platyrrhini — flat nose, New World); Old World (Cercopithecinae — narrow nose, Old World).
Apes (no tail): gorilla, chimpanzee, orangutan, gibbon; humans are great apes (hominids).
Human evolution: Australopithecus (bipedal, small brain) → Homo habilis (tool use) → Homo erectus (fire, larger brain) → Homo neanderthalensis → Homo sapiens.
Key adaptations: bipedalism, enlarged brain, loss of body hair, development of language and culture.
Fossil evidence: Lucy (Australopithecus afarensis, Ethiopia, 1974); Homo habilis (Olduvai Gorge); Neanderthals (Europe/Asia).
Molecular evidence: human-chimpanzee DNA similarity (~98.8%) and shared mitochondrial Eve; both lineages diverged ~6–7 million years ago.
confusion: Humans are NOT apes; we are hominids (great apes) within the family Hominidae, but a distinct lineage.
Australopithecus was bipedal but had a small brain (~400–500 mL); the brain enlarged later in Homo.
Homo habilis (the "handy man") made stone tools; Homo erectus (the "upright man") controlled fire and left Africa.
Neanderthals were NOT primitive; they made tools, buried dead, and had larger brains on average than modern humans.
Bipedalism (upright walking) evolved BEFORE the large brain — a key sequence in human evolution.
Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor (~6–7 Ma); we did not evolve "from" chimpanzees.

universalFacts: Lucy (Australopithecus afarensis, 1974, Ethiopia) is ~3.2 million years old and bipedal.
Humans and chimpanzees share ~98.8% of their DNA.
Homo neanderthalensis (Neanderthals) lived in Europe and Asia until ~40,000 years ago.
The "Out of Africa" model: modern humans originated in Africa ~200,000 years ago and spread worldwide.
examples: Australopithecus afarensis (Lucy) — bipedal, small brain, ~3.2 Ma.
Homo habilis — "handy man," made Oldowan stone tools, ~2.4 Ma.
Homo erectus — "upright man," controlled fire, larger brain, left Africa ~1.8 Ma.
Homo neanderthalensis — robust, large brain, cold-adapted, extinct ~40,000 years ago.
Homo sapiens — modern human; language, culture, agriculture (~10,000 years ago).

enrichedContent.summary: Humans (Homo sapiens) are primates in the family Hominidae. Evolution proceeded from bipedal Australopithecus through tool-using Homo habilis and fire-using Homo erectus to Neanderthals and modern Homo sapiens. Key adaptations include bipedalism, brain enlargement, loss of body hair, and the development of language and culture. Fossil evidence (Lucy, Homo habilis, Neanderthals) and molecular evidence (~98.8% DNA similarity with chimpanzees) confirm that humans share a common ancestor with other primates ~6–7 million years ago.

exercises.question: Why is bipedalism considered to have evolved before the large brain in human ancestors?
steps: Fossils (Lucy) show upright walking with small brain
Bipedalism freed hands for tool use
Larger brains evolved later in Homo species
